title: IAM Identity Center & Workforce Federation
summary: Single sign-on for employees across many accounts using an existing identity provider.
services: AWS Directory Service (AD Connector, AWS Managed Microsoft AD)
tldr: Employees + many accounts + existing IdP = **IAM Identity Center**. It is the default answer for workforce SSO in an organization.
Access is given by assigning **groups** to **permission sets** in target accounts. Each permission set becomes a role in each account.
Identity source can be the built-in directory, **Active Directory** (via AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD), or an external SAML 2.0 IdP such as Okta or Entra ID with **SCIM** provisioning.

keyFacts.text: Automatically provisions and deprovisions users and groups from an external IdP, so joiners, movers and leavers are updated without manual steps.
A proxy that forwards sign-in requests to your on-premises domain controllers. Nothing is synchronized to AWS; users keep their existing AD credentials.
**Attributes for access control** pass IdP attributes (department, project) as session tags, so one permission set can compare them with resource tags.
`aws configure sso` and `aws sso login` give developers short-lived CLI credentials, replacing IAM user access keys.

traps: **Cognito** is for customer (app) identities, not employees signing in to AWS accounts.
Creating IAM users in each account and syncing passwords with scripts is never the answer for SSO.
One permission set per project defeats ABAC; use one permission set with tag conditions instead.
Simple AD is not Microsoft AD and can't connect to an on-premises domain.
